name: Body Scan
intro: Find a comfortable position. Lying down is ideal, but sitting works too.
Close your eyes. Let your arms rest at your sides.
We're going to move through your body, one area at a time.
There's nothing to do except notice. No fixing. Just feeling.
body: Bring your attention to the top of your head.
Notice any sensation there. Tingling. Warmth. Pressure. Or nothing at all.
Now move to your forehead. Is it smooth, or are you furrowing without realizing?
Soften it. Let your eyebrows drop. Let the space between them widen.
Move to your eyes. Let them rest heavy in their sockets. No effort to see.
Now your jaw. This is where many of us hold the world.
Let your teeth part slightly. Let your tongue rest soft in your mouth.
Feel your neck. Both sides. The front. The back where it meets your skull.
Let your neck be long and free. No holding.
Roll your awareness down to your shoulders. Let them melt downward, away from your ears.
Move into your arms. Your upper arms. Your elbows. Your forearms.
Feel the weight of each arm. Let them be completely heavy.
Now your hands. Your palms. Each finger.
Notice if they're clenched. If so, simply open them. Let them be loose.
Your hands do so much. Let them rest now.
Bring your attention to your chest. Feel it rise and fall.
Don't change your breathing. Just watch it.
Move to your belly. Let it be soft. No need to hold it in.
Feel your lower back. The curve of your spine.
If there's tension, breathe into it. Imagine your breath reaching that exact spot.
Now your legs. Your thighs. Heavy against the surface beneath you.
Your knees. Your shins. Your calves.
Down to your ankles. Your feet. The soles of your feet.
Each toe. One by one. Feel them. Thank them.
Your whole body has been scanned. You are here. Fully present. Fully alive.
closing: Now feel your body as one whole. Not parts. One connected being.
You've given every part of yourself attention. That's a form of love.
Take three deep breaths. Each one a little deeper than the last.
Begin to move gently. Small stretches. Whatever feels good.
When you're ready, open your eyes. You've come home to yourself.
